rationale: A wins because it keeps the architecture cleaner and the proof burden honest. “Bumble still says women message first. Now AI can write that message for them.” is a real contradiction sitting inside the supplied facts. B has good bones, but it decorates the same idea into “Is Bumble's Women-First Model Still Feminist?” and then wanders into “Bumble is the highest-profile dating platform” without evidence. That is how a workable angle turns into a fact-check cleanup job.
gaps_in_A: “AI matchmaking just went mainstream” and “category-standard feature” overstate the supplied facts; A admits it needs outside evidence, but the headline already spends the claim.
“the company's public answer to the falling stock price and user decline” treats Bumble's motive as established; the update only says the relaunch follows those declines.
“its ‘authentic,’ women-first model” slightly smuggles in brand language; authenticity is in the user criticism, not a supplied Bumble claim.
gaps_in_B: “Is Bumble's Women-First Model Still Feminist?” imports a feminist/gender-politics frame the update did not supply. It may be pitchable, but it needs proof, not vibes.
“Bumble is the highest-profile dating platform to deploy AI matchmaking and AI-assisted message writing at scale” is invented altitude. No scale, peer set, or category ranking was supplied.
“user backlash is already on record” overstates the fact pattern; the update says some users have criticized AI in dating as inauthentic, not necessarily this Bumble relaunch.
“The relaunch is the stated answer to the subscriber slide” invents company attribution. If Bumble did not state that, do not put words in its mouth.
